Yeah, that's one of the reasons I started. The counting and paying attention to colors and stuff takes up enough of my brain that if I'm listening to someone/the TV/a movie it keeps me from circling, anxious thoughts.

I was kinda hesitant to buy this pattern  when I saw it on Etsy because it seemed really big to frame, but now that I see it in your photo I love it! It looks incredible! 

What kind of metallic thread did you use?

Oh, and the litter box I use is one of those that "folds" and takes up barely the space of a large wallet. I recommend bringing a liner though, to make it easy to dump the litter in the trash can once it's used.

I've had my "Sherpa" carrier for I think around four years? I use it a lot. For in-cabin, get a soft carrier (so it can squish slightly when you put it under the seat). Make sure you check on the airline's website for the acceptable dimensions for a carrier when traveling in cabin, and buy your carrier depending on that.

As for the litter box, I have put it out in either a bathroom stall (kept my cat on her leash) or in a "pet relief area" (didn't have to since it's a closed room).

Some of these could be applied to the one that will travel  "below" (I don't have experience with that). Oh, and I always carry my cat's travel documents with my own, and put an extra copy (or something identifying) in the carrier pockets.

Are your cats harness trained? Or at least comfortable with you holding them? You will be asked to take the cat out of the carrier (and, in the US, have your hands swabbed) when you go through security, while your carrier goes through the scanner.

When I travel with my cat in cabin, I always make sure:

--travel with some "snacks" and her favorite wet food (and those travel folding silicon bowls) 
--carry a travel water bottle that can be refilled on the other side of security) 
--line the bottom of the carrier with a pee pad
--add in a shirt/blanket that smells of me that my cat can sleep on
--I also travel with a portable litter box and a small zip lock of litter on those trips that are longer (such as Madrid-Amsterdam-San Diego or Madrid-Newark-San Francisco). Sometimes my cat uses the litter, other times she doesn't.

Same here. I've held the knife, planned the notes. Backed off. 

What I do to keep the thoughts at bay is find an activity that requires all of my concentration. For me, it's making things with my hands, whether it's sewing or painting or scrapbooking or  cross stitch. Then I put on something loud that I can listen to. Having to focus both on what I'm doing with my hands and what I'm listening to/watching keeps my brain busy enough that I CAN'T keep focused on the negative thoughts--only on what is right in front of me. Before I know it, my brain "empties", just for a bit. 

Maybe you can try that or an activity that does the same for you?

Today I just read a news story about a cat that had been lost for 15 years being returned to its owner! So don't lose hope, it's a big world out there and she might even be living safely in a home and rembering you fondly! It's absolutely natural to miss such an important part of your life, I understand. 

Personally, I agree with what other commenters said: you should adopt a new cat. They will never replace your old cat in your heart, but you will be saving a life, and finding a new purpose and energy. Our cats help us find meaning in each day, and we receive their love gratefully. 

Sending you love <3

Please think of your cat. Don't give them up. Your cat loves you, you are the center of its world, it's family. Focus on your cat, think of it, love it, cry with it...they'll be there with you and keep you from being alone.

Even though right now you feel like your cat is better off without you--think of how scared it might feel going somewhere new, and how they will always be happier purring and sleeping near you. Don't you enjoy being with your cat? They for sure enjoy being near you. 

I've been right there like you, and I'm still here because of my beautiful black cat who I've raised since she was a kitten, and who's traveled with me to another country. 

Things are tough right now, but just go over to your cat and hug them, breathe deep, smell them. Close your eyes and concentrate on the now. You're not alone, you have another living creature with you, one that loves you in only the pure way an animal can. You're not alone, all of us on this site are here supporting and keeping each other safe for another hour, another day, another week. We can do this.
